title: Cryogenic control electronics for quantum processors
bottleneck: Quantum processors need control electronics at millikelvin temperatures, but conventional CMOS dissipates too much heat and behaves unpredictably at cryogenic temperatures (carrier freeze-out, kink effects). Running thousands of control lines from room temperature into a dilution refrigerator creates a wiring and thermal bottleneck that scales worse than the qubits. Cryo-CMOS and superconducting control logic exist but lack the density and maturity for million-qubit systems.
why_it_blocks: Control scaling is the hidden wall for quantum computing: qubits are useless without classical electronics to drive them, and the fridge can't host today's control racks. Fault-tolerant quantum computing waits on cryogenic electronics as much as on better qubits.
current_state: Cryo-CMOS controllers from Intel, Google, and others demonstrate multiplexed control of tens to hundreds of qubits. Scaling to thousands of channels within millikelvin thermal budgets is unsolved.
